newsitem.title: UK: Hambros awaits independent CWS probe report.
newsitem.headline: Hambros awaits independent CWS probe report.

text.p: British investment banking group Hambros Plc said on Wednesday it was still awaiting the independent report it had commissioned into its role in the failed takeover of Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) by 31-year-old entrepreneur Andrew Regan.

"We will take as soon as possible any action that needs to be taken to ensure that we preserve, and then enhance, the good name which is so important to us," chief executive Sir Chips Keswick said in Hambros' annual results statement.

Keswick said he believed the report would enable the bank, which apologised unreservedly to supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group CWS for its involvement in the discredited takeover bid, to put the matter behind it.
"We believe that this will enable us to put the matter behind us and continue the momentum of current business development efforts in corporate finance as well as the rest of the bank," he said.

CWS dropped legal action against Hambros after its apology and a substantial financial settlement. Hambros has severed its links with Regan, his Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica and the Galileo special bidding vehicle.

It appointed City law firm Norton Rose to undertake the probe into the affair and Peter Large, the senior corporate financier responsible for the bid has asked to be relieved of his executive responsibilities to enable him to concentrate on the investigation.
